paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose your university is organizing a forum on the development of students’ cross-cultural communication abilities. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您的大学正在组织一个关于学生跨文化沟通能力发展的论坛。你现在要写一篇文章来表达你的观点。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Psychologists have long been interested in how we construct our identities and the sorts of strategies that we use to present ourselves in society. New findings suggest that the kinds of 26 and strategic self-presentation behaviour we see in adults appear at a much younger age than 27 known.
paragraphs.translationZh: 心理学家长期以来一直对我们如何构建自己的身份以及我们在社会上展示自己的策略感兴趣。新的研究结果表明，我们在成年人中看到的复杂且战略性的自我呈现行为出现的年龄比我们之前所知的要年轻得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Research shows that a child’s awareness of social standing comes from adults. Like grown-ups, kids want to be 28 by those they admire. Interactive experiences may provide opportunities for children to learn about what 29 a desirable reputation and the kinds of strategies that are effective for 30 a good reputation in their social environment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究表明，孩子的社会地位意识来自于成人。像成年人一样，孩子们希望被他们钦佩的人接受。互动体验可以为孩子们提供机会，让他们了解什么是理想的声誉，以及在社交环境中有效建立良好声誉的策略。

paragraphs.sourceText: Five-year-olds aren’t just aware of their reputations, they also behave strategically to alter their outward image. They will 31 their behaviour in order to appear moral or socially good in the eyes of key observers. While we know that adults use a large variety of attributes to manage and create impressions, we don’t yet know whether children 32 and use the fact that different attributes are valuable at different times to different 33 . It’s important for us to further consider where in this process children succeed in controlling their reputation and where they 34 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 五岁的孩子不仅意识到自己的声誉，而且还通过策略性的行为来改变自己的外在形象。他们会改变自己的行为，以便在关键观察者眼中显得道德或社会良好。虽然我们知道成年人使用各种各样的属性来管理和创造印象，但我们还不知道孩子们是否理解并利用这样一个事实：不同的属性在不同的时间对不同的受众来说是有价值的。对我们来说，进一步考虑孩子在这个过程中哪些地方成功地控制了自己的声誉以及哪些地方遇到了困难，这一点很重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: A question to think about is, “What happens even earlier than age five?” Children don’t just show up to the first day of kindergarten and have the idea of reputation pop 35 into existence. The logical question to ask is, “What happens even earlier?”
paragraphs.translationZh: 需要思考的一个问题是，“五岁之前会发生什么？”孩子们并不是在进入幼儿园的第一天就突然产生了声誉的想法。合乎逻辑的问题是：“更早发生了什么？”

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Getting young minds into design
paragraphs.translationZh: 让年轻人参与设计

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology. These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 最近，英国一个领先的设计联合会警告称，最新数据显示，学习设计和技术的学生人数下降了近 10%，英国可能面临创意技能短缺。这些数据显示，去年参加设计与技术考试的学生人数从 204,788 人下降到 185,279 人，下降了 10%。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain’s hugely successful arts and creative industries. He said, “We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation (动画制作) and special effects.” He added: “Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 创意产业联合会首席执行官约翰·坎普夫纳 (John Kampfner) 认为，这一数字的下降对英国非常成功的艺术和创意产业的技能管道产生了令人担忧的影响。他说：“我们在动画制作和特效等许多工作领域已经出现了技能短缺。”他补充道：“工程学需要类似的创造性和技术技能，也存在招聘问题。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support. However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased. With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children’s toy called “Dazzle Racer”. An automotive cylinder (圆柱体), it included a wind-up, elastic (有弹性的)-band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled, and lots of stickers. It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 许多其他设计师和建筑师对英国公司未来本土人才的供应表示担忧，行业机构指出缺乏基层支持。然而，如果这些设计师今年早些时候参观了伦敦设计博物馆商店，他们的担忧可能会得到缓解。只要花 10 英镑，他们就可以购买一款名为“Dazzle Racer”的迷人儿童玩具。它是一个汽车圆柱体（圆柱体），包括一个发条、有弹性的带动力机构、最少的零件（全部 100% 可回收）以及大量贴纸。这很有趣、简单、引人注目并且非常原创。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Well, you’d expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different. Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum’s 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 嗯，你会期望设计博物馆委托制作一些有趣的物品，但这个不同。该玩具由芬奇利天主教高中 (Finchley Catholic High School) 的六名 9 年级和 10 年级男生设计，是该博物馆 2015 年 Design Ventura 竞赛的获奖作品，该竞赛通过挑战他们为设计博物馆商店开发一种新的创意、可持续和商业上可行的产品，将设计业务带入生活，为 13 至 16 岁的学生提供帮助，并吸引了全国数百件参赛作品。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) “We did Design Ventura in my previous school,” says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School’s design technology curriculum leader. “Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) “我们在以前的学校开设了 Design Ventura，”芬奇利天主教高中设计技术课程负责人 Liam Hourican 说道。 “四年前我转学时，我把它引入了这里，因为它有助于培养很多技能。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The theme for last year’s competition was “Move”, and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea. Each participating school may submit just one proposal. “It’s the taking part and doing the work which is important,” he says. “And I never dreamt we’d win.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 去年比赛的主题是“移动”，Hourican 从三个小组开始，在午休时间和放学后进行工作，然后选择最具创新想法的小组。每所参与学校只能提交一份提案。 “重要的是参与和完成工作，”他说。 “我从未梦想过我们会赢。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project — funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be — is the biggest event in the museum’s calendar. “We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since,” she says. “Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject,” she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 设计博物馆的学习主管凯瑟琳·里特曼·史密斯 (Catherine Ritman Smith) 预计今年将有约 10,000 名 13 至 16 岁的参与者参加，并表示该项目由德意志银行资助，作为其青年参与计划 Born To Be 的一部分，是博物馆日历上最大的活动。 “2010 年，我们与大约 800 名年轻人一起创办了 Design Ventura，此后它一直在稳步发展，”她说。 “老师们喜欢它，因为这些技能都是可以转移的，而且它有助于验证设计作为一门学科的价值，”她解释道，并告诉我到目前为止已有近 600 所学校参加了。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) So how does the competition work? A single-word theme is announced in the summer. This year it is “Change”. Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop. Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea. Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers. An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 那么比赛是如何进行的呢？夏季将公布一个单字主题。今年是“变”。学校与团体合作，用简单的材料制作出富有想象力的产品设计理念，这些产品在设计博物馆商店可以卖到 10 英镑。参与学校将在 11 月之前进行注册并最终提交他们的设计理念。在此过程中，设计师为教师提供培训和支持，并为学生提供辅导。额外的奖励是获奖者在第二年春天看到他们的设计出售。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran. Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees. The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions — they changed the product’s name, for example.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) Hourican 和他的学生们在博物馆度过了一整天的美好回忆，他们被选为 10 所入围学校之一，向包括设计师 Jasper Conran 在内的评审团展示他们的想法。然后，他们与肖尔迪奇的 Kin 设计工作室合作，在学校会见了设计师，并与德意志银行员工共进午餐。学生们帮助做出决定，并进行了大量讨论——例如，他们更改了产品的名称。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) “One of the really useful things about this competition,” says Hourican, “is that there’s a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game.” Profits go to charity. “The winning team chooses where it wants the profits to go,” says Ritman Smith. “The Finchley Catholic High School product raised about £1,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital.” Winning entries in past years have included a make-your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) “这场比赛真正有用的事情之一，”胡里坎说，“是有商业元素，因为产品正在真正销售，男孩们必须学习预算和营销，以及设计他们的游戏。”利润捐给慈善机构。 “获胜的团队会选择他们希望利润流向的地方，”里特曼·史密斯说。 “芬奇利天主教高中的产品为大奥蒙德街医院筹集了约 1,000 英镑。”过去几年的获奖作品包括一款名为“Dove Bunting”的自制布料套件，以及一款名为“Badoiiing”的钱包大小的三重旅行游戏，两端都有目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free. Among them is architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects. He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 学校无需支付任何费用即可参与 Design Ventura；专业设计师免费提供服务。其中包括建筑师阿西夫·汗(Asif Khan)，他是设计博物馆的受托人，曾在博物馆担任驻场设计师，帮助新兴建筑师。他最近受委托设计位于史密斯菲尔德的新伦敦博物馆大楼。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition’s judges. “I’m very keen to encourage young people,” she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science. “Now that design education is limited in the curriculum, I’m all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life,” says Cleaver. “And the judging day is terrific fun. Some of these students are very imaginative. One group presented their idea in the form of a puppet show and we see some marvelous demonstration models. I’m always impressed by the levels of confidence and the support the students get from their teachers.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 另一位是电视节目主持人兼室内设计师 Naomi Cleaver，她是比赛的评委之一。 “我非常热衷于鼓励年轻人，”她说，并观察到设计汇集了文学、艺术、历史、地理和科学等其他学科。 “既然设计教育在课程中受到限制，我完全赞成像 Design Ventura 这样的竞赛，这有助于将标准课程变为现实，”Cleaver 说。 “评审日非常有趣。其中一些学生非常富有想象力。一组以木偶剧的形式展示了他们的想法，我们看到了一些精彩的演示模型。学生们从老师那里得到的自信和支持总是给我留下了深刻的印象。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Ritman Smith adds: “Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we’ve heard of departments closing in some schools. We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M) Ritman Smith 补充道：“设计技术已经成为一门难以论证的学科，我们听说一些学校关闭了院系。我们发现，如果学生在九年级参加 Design Ventura，可能会成为促使他们选择中等教育普通证书课程的触发因素，因此我们正在帮助保持对工业和创业至关重要的东西的活力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. During the course of preparing for Design Ventura, teachers receive training and support while students get tutoring from designers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 在设计文图拉的准备过程中，教师接受培训和支持，学生则得到设计师的辅导。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. A visit to the Design Museum shop in London can reduce the designers’ fears about the future supply of talents educated in Britain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37.参观伦敦设计博物馆商店可以减少设计师对未来在英国接受教育的人才供应的担忧。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. One of Design Ventura’s judges says the competition adds vigour to the standard curriculum in schools.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. Design Ventura 的一位评委表示，这项竞赛为学校的标准课程增添了活力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Enrollment in Design and Technology decreased by nearly ten percent last year in the UK.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 去年英国设计与技术专业的入学人数下降了近百分之十。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Participation of ninth graders in Design Ventura can motivate them to choose design technology as their subject.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 九年级学生参与 Design Ventura 可以激励他们选择设计技术作为他们的科目。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Design Ventura is welcomed by teachers because it helps to prove the worth of design as a school subject.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. Design Ventura 受到教师的欢迎，因为它有助于证明设计作为学校科目的价值。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The schools don’t have to pay anything to take part in the Design Ventura competition.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 学校无需支付任何费用即可参加 Design Ventura 竞赛。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Participants in Design Ventura are challenged to create sustainable and marketable products.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. Design Ventura 参与者面临的挑战是创造可持续且适销对路的产品。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Students benefit from Design Ventura because they can learn about budgeting and marketing in addition to game design.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 学生从 Design Ventura 中受益，因为除了游戏设计之外，他们还可以学习预算和营销。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. According to an officer of the Creative Industries Federation, there is difficulty now in recruiting engineers in the UK.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 据创意产业联合会的一位官员称，现在在英国招聘工程师很困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 新的研究表明，大熊猫可能面临灭绝的危险，因为它们太舒服了。专家表示，太多的快乐会阻止熊寻找新的伴侣。

paragraphs.sourceText: Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by “reducing or fragmenting their natural habitats”, The Times reported. But the new research suggests that a “modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation” may actually help preserve panda populations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，环保人士长期以来一直认为，在熊附近修建道路或房屋可能会“减少或破坏它们的自然栖息地”，从而威胁它们的生存。但新的研究表明，“适度的不适和分裂”实际上可能有助于保护大熊猫种群。

paragraphs.sourceText: The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究是由密歇根州立大学的科学家进行的。研究得出的结论是，如果大熊猫发现自己的栖息地太舒适，它们就不会四处寻找新的伴侣，从而导致缺乏重要的遗传多样性。

paragraphs.sourceText: For their study — outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology — the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在《保护生物学》杂志上的一篇论文中概述的研究中，研究小组研究了中国大熊猫种群中的遗传多样性和传播情况。研究发现，完美宜居栖息地的理想水平仅为 80% 的区域，其余区域要么过于恶劣，要么过于受人类活动影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: The experts concluded that pandas should ideally “be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don’t want to move around and find new mates”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家们得出的结论是，理想情况下，大熊猫应该“足够快乐，能够茁壮成长，但又不能太满足，以至于不想四处走动并寻找新的伴侣”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this “sweet spot” are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们对《卫报》所描述的“最佳位置”的结论符合所谓的金发姑娘原则：可以有适量的东西。这一概念已应用于从发展心理学到经济学和工程学的广泛学科。

paragraphs.sourceText: Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 牛津大学保护生物学教授克劳迪奥·西莱罗（Claudio Sillero）告诉该报，新发现的影响可能超出大熊猫保护范围。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes,” said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. “It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “大多数吃肉的大型动物生活在日益分散的环境中，”没有参与这项研究的西莱罗说。 “它们与人类努力之间的混乱关系很可能会导致更多的动物分散或迁徙得更远，并可能导致更大的遗传连通性和增强的种群持久性。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近对大熊猫的统计发现，野生大熊猫数量已超过 1,800 只，将它们列入易危物种名单，但并非濒危物种。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. But what about those of us who don’t have a natural talent? We’ve been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. But with the release of Angela Duckworth’s Grit, we are given a new key to success.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于那些天生具有天赋的人来说，感觉好像他们不需要真正的努力就能出类拔萃。但对于我们这些没有天赋的人来说呢？我们一生都被告知，如果你努力工作，你也能成功。但随着安吉拉·达克沃斯 (Angela Duckworth) 的《勇气》(Grit) 的发行，我们获得了成功的新钥匙。

paragraphs.sourceText: “As much as talent counts, effort counts twice,” says Duckworth in Grit. She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence. Even if you have natural talent, it’s nothing without grit.
paragraphs.translationZh: 达克沃斯在《勇气》中说道：“天赋固然重要，但努力更重要。”她引入了一个新概念：天赋可能被高估，如果你想要真正的成功，你需要的是勇气，激情与坚持的完美结合。即使你有天赋，但如果没有毅力，那也是一事无成。

paragraphs.sourceText: Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. When we think about attaining success — whether it’s landing that job or learning that new skill — our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part — and you must be perfect at all of them. Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn’t the goal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 达克沃斯说，毅力是成功与失败的区别。一个有毅力的人比没有毅力的人更有可能成功。当我们考虑获得成功时——无论是找到工作还是学习新技能——我们的思想立即就会被我们必须首先学习的所有东西所困扰。如果你想要这份新工作，你必须学习工作技能，然后是面试技巧，然后是着装部分——而且你必须在所有这些方面都做到完美。毅力是不同的，因为它告诉我们完美不是目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. Think about it: what’s something you’ve always wanted to do, but gave up because you “don’t have the skills for it”? What’s something you love but aren’t good at?
paragraphs.translationZh: 毅力可以消除我们肩上不合理的期望。勇气告诉我们，这扇门比我们最初想象的要大。毅力让我们能够重新定义我们的目标。想一想：有什么事情是你一直想做却因为“没有能力”而放弃的？有什么事情是你喜欢但不擅长的？

paragraphs.sourceText: The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try. Effort means more than your natural ability. Even if you haven’t mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams. She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything. If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit.
paragraphs.translationZh: 坚毅的真正作用是拥有持续的热情并不断尝试。努力不仅仅意味着你的自然能力。即使您尚未掌握某项技能，毅力也会告诉您，如果您能将激情转化为行动，您仍然可以获得成功。在某种程度上，达克沃斯给那些关闭梦想之门的人们带来了新的希望。她是说你有可能完成任何事情。如果一开始失败了，那就勇敢地再试一次。

options.sourceText: They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat.
options.reflowSourceText: They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat.

options.sourceText: They may cease to exist as a result of enjoying too good a life.
options.reflowSourceText: They may cease to exist as a result of enjoying too good a life.

options.reflowSourceText: It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity.

options.sourceText: Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening.
options.reflowSourceText: Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening.

options.sourceText: Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas.

options.sourceText: Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species.
options.reflowSourceText: Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species.

options.reflowSourceText: Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals.

options.sourceText: Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals.
options.reflowSourceText: Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals.

options.sourceText: They seem to outdo others without hard work.
options.reflowSourceText: They seem to outdo others without hard work.

options.sourceText: They appear to know all the secrets to success.
options.reflowSourceText: They appear to know all the secrets to success.

options.sourceText: They feel it only too logical to succeed.
options.reflowSourceText: They feel it only too logical to succeed.
